subject: Logic
title: Schelling Points
description: A quick, practical guide to Schelling Points.

hook.text: You have to meet someone in New York with no way to communicate. Where do you go? Grand Central, noon—most people agree.

buildup.text: A Schelling point is a solution people converge on without communication, using shared cultural expectations.

discovery.text: Thomas Schelling showed that coordination depends on shared context, not just logic.

twist.text: There's nothing logically special about Grand Central. But its prominence makes it the obvious mutual guess.

climax.text: In negotiations, norms, and conflicts, Schelling points shape outcomes because people gravitate to the obvious.

punchline.text: The obvious answer wins when nobody can talk.

quiz.question: What is a Schelling point?
options: A solution people converge on through shared expectations
